title: WORKSHEET 40
subject: Used to / Would / Be used to
subjectVi: Ngữ pháp bài 40: Used to / Would / Be used to

sections.instruction: Complete the sentences using USED TO or BE USED TO:

questions.prompt: I [gap] (live) in Finland, but now I live in France.
acceptedAnswers: used to live
questions.explanation: used to + V: past state that is no longer true

questions.prompt: He [gap] (sit) in the back of the classroom, but now he prefers to sit in the front row.
acceptedAnswers: used to sit

questions.prompt: When I was a child, I [gap] (play) games with my friends in a big field near my house after school every day.
acceptedAnswers: used to play

questions.prompt: It’s hard for my children to stay inside on a cold, rainy day. They [gap] (play) outside in the big field near our house. They play there almost every day.
acceptedAnswers: are used to playing
questions.explanation: be used to + V-ing: accustomed to (now)

questions.prompt: People [gap] (believe) that the world was flat.
acceptedAnswers: used to believe
questions.explanation: used to + V: past belief, no longer true

questions.prompt: Trains [gap] (be) the main means of cross-continental travel. Today, most people take airplanes for long-distance travel.
acceptedAnswers: used to be

questions.prompt: Ms. Stanton’s job requires her to travel extensively throughout the world. She [gap] (travel) by plane.
acceptedAnswers: is used to traveling|is used to travelling
questions.explanation: be used to + V-ing: accustomed to

questions.prompt: You and I are from different cultures. You [gap] (have) fish for breakfast. I [gap] (have) cheese and bread for breakfast.
acceptedAnswers: are used to having / am used to having
questions.explanation: be used to + V-ing: accustomed to

questions.prompt: What [gap] (do) on summer days when you were a child?
acceptedAnswers: did you use to do
questions.explanation: question: did + subject + use to + V

questions.prompt: Bill lives alone. He doesn’t mind this, because he [gap] (live) alone.
acceptedAnswers: is used to living
questions.explanation: be used to + V-ing: accustomed to

questions.prompt: Tom [gap] (drink) a lot of coffee. Now he prefers tea.
acceptedAnswers: used to drink

questions.prompt: I have to work hard. This is not a problem for me. I have always worked hard. So I [gap] (work) hard.
acceptedAnswers: am used to working
questions.explanation: be used to + V-ing: accustomed to

questions.prompt: Some friends of yours have just moved into a flat on a busy street. It is very noisy. They will [gap] the noise.
acceptedAnswers: get used to
questions.explanation: get used to: become accustomed to

questions.prompt: When we were children, we [gap] (swim) every day.
acceptedAnswers: used to swim

questions.prompt: I haven’t been to the cinema for ages now. We [gap] (go) a lot.
acceptedAnswers: used to go

questions.prompt: Dennis gave up smoking two years ago. He [gap] (smoke).
acceptedAnswers: used to smoke

sections.instruction: Rewrite the sentences using USED TO: (Example: When she was a child, she lived in a small village. → When she was a child, she used to live in a small village.)

questions.prompt: When he was a young man, he enjoyed playing basketball.
acceptedAnswers: When he was a young man, he used to enjoy playing basketball.
He used to enjoy playing basketball when he was a young man.
questions.explanation: used to + V: past habit / state

questions.prompt: In ancient Rome, wall paintings were a popular form of advertising.
acceptedAnswers: In ancient Rome, wall paintings used to be a popular form of advertising.
Wall paintings used to be a popular form of advertising in ancient Rome.

questions.prompt: Before she learned to read, her parents read stories to her.
acceptedAnswers: Before she learned to read, her parents used to read stories to her.
Her parents used to read stories to her before she learned to read.

questions.prompt: Before he came to Ankara, life was cheap in Turkey.
acceptedAnswers: Before he came to Ankara, life used to be cheap in Turkey.
Life used to be cheap in Turkey before he came to Ankara.

questions.prompt: Jim spoke German at school, but he has now forgotten.
acceptedAnswers: Jim used to speak German at school, but he has now forgotten.
Jim used to speak German at school, but he has now forgotten it.
Jim used to speak German at school, but now he has forgotten.
questions.explanation: used to + V: past habit, no longer true

questions.prompt: Susan was a nurse before she got married and raised a family.
acceptedAnswers: Susan used to be a nurse before she got married and raised a family.
Before she got married and raised a family, Susan used to be a nurse.

questions.prompt: Sally played tennis when abroad, but she prefers swimming now.
acceptedAnswers: Sally used to play tennis when abroad, but she prefers swimming now.
Sally used to play tennis when she was abroad, but she prefers swimming now.
Sally used to play tennis when abroad, but now she prefers swimming.

questions.prompt: Before they bought their house, they lived in an apartment.
acceptedAnswers: Before they bought their house, they used to live in an apartment.
They used to live in an apartment before they bought their house.

questions.prompt: While she was going to university, she worked in a doctor’s office.
acceptedAnswers: While she was going to university, she used to work in a doctor's office.
She used to work in a doctor's office while she was going to university.

questions.prompt: Before he married his second wife, he was quite happy.
acceptedAnswers: Before he married his second wife, he used to be quite happy.
He used to be quite happy before he married his second wife.

sections.instruction: Complete the text about Ziggy Starr when she was a child using USED TO / DIDN’T USE TO and the verbs in brackets: (Example: I didn’t use to have (not have) many friends when I was a child.)

questions.prompt: I didn’t use to have many friends when I was a child so I [gap] (play) with my toys all day.
acceptedAnswers: used to play

questions.prompt: I [gap] (worry) about things a lot but I [gap] (not bite) my nails or suck my thumb.
acceptedAnswers: used to worry / didn't use to bite

questions.prompt: I remember that I [gap] (cry) a lot and I [gap] (be) really afraid of the dark.
acceptedAnswers: used to cry / used to be
questions.explanation: used to + V: past habit / state

sections.instruction: Complete the text using USED TO and the verbs in the box: (Example: We used to wear school uniform.)
sections.contextText:
School has changed since I was a student. We used to wear school uniform and I didn’t like that very much.
(Sentences 1–4)
Some of them were impossible! I think school is easier now than it was 50 years ago.

questions.prompt: We [gap] a lot of lessons and most of them were difficult.
acceptedAnswers: used to have

questions.prompt: We [gap] homework every day.
acceptedAnswers: used to do

questions.prompt: We [gap] lots of books and we [gap] everything by heart.
acceptedAnswers: used to read / used to learn

questions.prompt: And our teachers [gap] us a lot of tests and examinations.
acceptedAnswers: used to give

sections.instruction: Use USED TO / WOULD (a repeated action in the past): (Example: I used to be very shy. Whenever a stranger came to our house, I would hide in a closet.)

questions.prompt: I remember my Aunt Susan very well. Every time she came to our house, she [gap] (give) me a big kiss and pinch my cheek.
acceptedAnswers: would give|used to give
questions.explanation: would / used to: repeated past action

questions.prompt: I [gap] (be) afraid of flying. My heart [gap] (start) pounding every time I stepped on a plane. But now I’m used to flying and enjoy it.
acceptedAnswers: used to be / would start|used to start
questions.explanation: states: used to only; actions: would / used to

questions.prompt: I got a new bicycle when I was ten. My friends [gap] (ask) to ride it, but for years I [gap] (let / never) anyone else use it.
acceptedAnswers: would ask|used to ask / would never let|never used to let|never let
questions.explanation: would / used to: repeated past action

questions.prompt: When my grandfather was a boy and had a cold, his mother [gap] (make) him go to bed. Then she [gap] (put) goose fat on his chest.
acceptedAnswers: would make|used to make / would put|used to put
questions.explanation: would / used to: repeated past action

questions.prompt: When I was a child, I [gap] (take) a flashlight to bed with me so that I could read comic books without my parents’ knowing about it.
acceptedAnswers: would take|used to take
questions.explanation: would / used to: repeated past action

questions.prompt: Last summer, my sister and I took a camping trip in the Rocky Mountains. It was a wonderful experience. Every morning, we [gap] (wake) up to the sound of singing birds. During the day, we [gap] (hike) through woods and along mountain streams.
acceptedAnswers: would wake / would hike
questions.explanation: would: repeated action during one past period

questions.prompt: I can remember Mrs. Sawyer’s fifth grade class well. When we arrived each morning, she [gap] (sit) at her desk. She [gap] (smile / always) and [gap] (say) hello to each student as he or she entered.
acceptedAnswers: would sit|would be sitting|used to sit / would always smile|always used to smile|used to always smile / would say|used to say|say
questions.explanation: would / used to: repeated past action

questions.prompt: When the bell rang, she [gap] (stand) up and [gap] (clear) her throat. That was our signal to be quiet. Class was about to begin.
acceptedAnswers: would stand|used to stand / would clear|used to clear|clear
questions.explanation: would / used to: repeated past action
